CORRECTION TO m60017, BLOCKER 2 — Alex is right, the D1 IS called for. My previous ruling was wrong; this one replaces it.

WHY: a Durable Object is BOUNDED (order of 10 GB per object — check the current CF limit before sizing). The ledger is append-only and credits never expire, so entries grow without end. An unbounded append-only record cannot live in a bounded object. Separately, a coop closing a period needs real queries across entries by member, period, class and contract type — that is SQL work, not DO storage work.

And this was already the design: BEB-1005 says settle writes BOTH the DO key (live balance) and a D1 row (the queryable audit). I contradicted our own spec.

THE SPLIT, ruled:
· DURABLE OBJECT = THE WALLET. Balance, escrow, atomicity, idempotency keys. Hot, small, bounded on purpose — it holds current state, not history.
· D1 = THE LEDGER OF RECORD. Every entry, append-only, double-entry, in micros, carrying member attribution, period, entry class, contract type, markup as its own line. This is what reports and settlement read.
· R2 = COLD ARCHIVE for closed periods when D1 approaches its own ceiling (D1 is also bounded — same order). Archive is not deletion and never voids a balance.

SO FOR BEB-3895: CREATE the D1, deliberately, with that schema — do not drop the binding and do not let codegen invent the shape. Name it once and everywhere; the name goes in the wrangler config and in the ticket, and it does not change again. If the name abilifi-sentinel is the one we want, create it under that name; if not, pick now and say so on the ticket.

WHY, so it is settled: two-phase reserve→settle is the spec of record (BEB-1005, refined by BEB-1059) and it is what the live service advertises at abilifi.net/health: contract "two-phase reserve+settle". rpc's single-shot model is the deviation and it dies. Rewrite abilifi-rpc to sentinel's shape, not the reverse.

SHAPE, keyed org_id:
· reserve { org_id, max_micros, idempotency_key } → { reqId }. rpc MUST capture reqId. A reserve that fails GATES the call — no model runs on a failed reserve (that is the BEB-1385 swallow bug: .catch(()=>{}) then proceed).
· settle { org_id, reqId, ttv, cfCost, contributorId, success } → takes ACTUAL, returns the rest. success=false refunds the whole reserve.
· org_id is the key; site and tenantId are accepted as aliases that RESOLVE to it and are never stored.
· AMOUNTS IN INTEGER MICROS — max_micros not max_cents. If rpc still speaks cents, convert at the edge of rpc, once, and never store a cent value.
· settle writes BOTH: the DO (balance, escrow) and D1 abilifi-sentinel 931ec8bb (the entry). Both or neither — a settle that writes one and not the other is the failure to guard against.
· markup is its OWN column on the entry, never folded into the charged amount.

You are right not to rush it. Real money: land it behind the existing serious-class review, prove it with ONE call, and the caller row in /ledger/:org_id is the evidence.

APPROVAL GATE — and note the shape carefully, this is the point.

Crediting a cleared-but-unrecorded payment is an ADMIN DECISION. A human approves it. A script never decides it.

BUT: build it as AUTOMATION WITH ONE GATE, not as a manual tool you automate later.

FLOW — automatic everywhere except step 4:
1. Reconcile runs on the tick.
2. Unmatched payments land in an APPROVAL QUEUE.
3. Each row shows payer, amount, date, provider ref, proposed action (grant / refund / ignore), and WHY it is unmatched.
4. **HUMAN APPROVES — the only manual step.** Button per row, plus approve-all.
5. On approval the grant issues via sentinel /grant; double-entry rows land with member attribution and period.
6. Approved AND rejected rows stay on the record with who approved and when. The approval is itself a ledger fact.

Why this way: when we later let a class auto-approve (exact amount match, known customer, under a threshold), that is a SETTINGS ROW on the queue — not a rebuild.

ADMIN FRAGS: reconcile-run · approval-queue · approve-row · reject-row · approval-log. MCP tool + codemode wrapper + Master Inventory row each (BEB-452/453). Members of the app node (BEB-3908). Same frag rules as the consumer screens — acceptance is the frag list, not a worker.

Client-scoped: every tenant gets a queue over THEIR unmatched payments. We are the first tenant. Our two payments are the first two rows — that is how they get settled.

SpecOps writes pages + journey BEFORE any mockup (m60571). Stripe read-only; the only write is the /grant after approval.

ADMIN ROW = PROOF + RETARGET. Two additions, both load-bearing.

**PROOF.** Every queue row carries a LINK TO THE COMPLETED PAYMENT at the provider — the Stripe dashboard URL for that charge, clickable, opens the real record. The admin approves against the source document, not our restatement of it. No working proof link = not approvable.

**USE THE STRIPE SDK.** Official SDK, read-only calls only. It looks, it confirms, it returns the charge. It never writes.

**ROW CONTENTS:** payer email · amount · currency · date · charge id · status · proof link · why unmatched · proposed action.

**RETARGET BEFORE APPROVE.** The admin can CHANGE THE IDAAS TARGET that receives the credit. The payer email is not automatically the right account — people pay from one address and use another, a client pays for a sub-client, a personal card pays a company account. So the row has an IDENTITY PICKER: search IDaaS, pick the account/org, then approve. We propose the best match; the human overrides.

**THEN CREDIT PROCESSES.** Approve fires sentinel /grant against the CHOSEN org_id. Double-entry, micros, member attribution, period. The approval, approver, chosen target and provider ref all land on the record so the chain reads back end to end.

FRAGS: reconcile-run · approval-queue · payment-proof-link · identity-picker · approve-row · reject-row · approval-log. MCP tool + codemode wrapper + Master Inventory row each. Client-scoped.
